subject: Fleet rebalancing & smoothing plan for NebulaHealth renewal
messages:
From: Elena Rios <elena.rios@nebulahealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Usage spike + upcoming renewal — need sizing guidance

Hi Soojin / Ben,

Hope you’re well. We’re getting close to the end of our pilot and early production traffic has increased faster than expected — roughly 2.5x week-over-week for the last three weeks. I attached a short export of token counts and p95 latency by model.

Our renewal window is Dec 1; we’re evaluating whether to: (A) increase committed GPUs now to avoid throttles, or (B) rely on burst/overcommit for the short term and revisit sizing after traffic stabilizes.

Key constraints:
- Procurement needs a recommended minimum commit and an alternate burst policy we can sign off on.
- We prefer predictable unit costs but can accept limited burst if it’s cheaper short-term.

Can you advise recommended commit sizing + an architecture suggestion (pool partitioning, overcommit ratio)? If you need more logs or traces, say the word and I’ll send them.

Thanks — Elena
Director, ML Platforms
NebulaHealth

Attachment: nebula_usage_q3_summary.pdf

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16T11:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Usage spike + upcoming renewal — need sizing guidance

Hi Elena — thanks for the data dump, that’s really helpful. Quick read: peak effective GPU hours are concentrated in a small number of long-chat sessions and a handful of high-embedding batches. We should be able to mitigate with two approaches depending on your risk/cost appetite.

Option A — Conservative commit (recommended for predictable apps):
- Commit a baseline of 18 A100-equivalent GPUs (estimated to cover steady-state at current p50/p95).
- Add a 20% burst pool (dedicated shared burst) with automatic fallback to hosted tier.
- Expected unit cost increase: ~14% vs current pay-as-you-go but lower throttling risk.

Option B — Aggressive overcommit (short-term cost-optimized):
- Commit 12 GPUs + overcommit policy 1.4x with continuous batching tuned for long chats.
- Allow scheduled autoscale windows for peak hours (02:00–06:00 PT warmups).
- Expect lower committed monthly cost but higher variance and potential throttling if growth continues.

To finalize we need: detailed 7-day token-by-session CSV (any PII redacted) and permission to pull your per-route latency/queue metrics from onboarding logs. If you’re comfortable, Ben can take the sample and produce a tranche-level forecast.

I’m attaching a starter pricing/workload model. I’ll loop in Marissa for commercial framing.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-17T14:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Usage spike + upcoming renewal — need sizing guidance

Elena — I pulled the sample you provided and ran it through our utilization model. High-level notes:
- The long-chat sessions (top 2% of sessions) account for ~48% of total token usage. Short requests are many but low token volume.
- Average concurrency for generation routes during peak windows is ~26 concurrent requests, median latency 140ms, p95 390ms.
- Embedding batch jobs run nightly with large variance; staggering would reduce peak amplifier.

Recommendation (technical):
1) Pool split: 14 GPUs for steady-state multitenant traffic; 6 GPUs in a burst tranche with pre-warmed KV caches for the top two models. This gives an operational ceiling of 20 GPUs immediately available and preserves warm caches during bursts.
2) Overcommit policy: conservative 1.25x on steady pool, 1.6x on the burst tranche (so bursts can oversubscribe for short windows). We model 95th percentile no-throttle for ~30 days under current growth at these levels.
3) Autoscale windows: scheduled warmups 30 minutes before known peak times reduces p95 by ~120ms.

I put a conservative monthly forecast and a stress-case in the attached spreadsheet and added a recommended amendment for the commitment (see tab: "Commit Options").

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Our preference is a mid-point: commit to 60% of the 30-day forecast with an agreed burst ceiling and an annualized escalator capped at 5%. If you can provide a DocuSign-ready amendment and a short SOW describing pool partitioning + warm-cache commitments, we’ll route internally.

Cc’ing Elena for sign-off on the technical piece.

Marcus / Elena — thanks for the clarity. Summary and proposed next steps below so we have a single agreed plan before legal/procurement drafts the amendment.

Agreed (proposal):
- Commit: 60% of the 30-day stress forecast (equivalent to 15 A100-e GPUs, per Ben’s conservative forecast tab).
- Burst: up to an additional 6 GPUs available as a burst tranche; billed at the burst rate after committed GPU-hours are exhausted.
- Overcommit policy: 1.25x on committed pool, 1.6x on burst tranche; Redwood will monitor and notify if sustained >4 weeks of burst usage is detected.
- Price escalator: capped at 5% annually.
- SOW: Redwood to provide a one-page SOW describing pool partitioning, warm-cache responsibilities, and autoscale windows.

Action items:
1) Redwood: draft commit amendment (DocuSign-ready) + one-page SOW and send to Marcus by end of day Thu 11/25. Attachment: commit_amendment_draft.docx (working draft).
2) Ben: finalize the workload tab with per-route assumptions and share the Drive link (done).
3) Nebula: confirm internal approval of 60% commit by Mon 11/29 so we can route legal.

If that timeline works I’ll get the amendment to you first thing Thurs and we can move to signature the following week.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
